Well, in most cases, encouraging and supporting children is seen as a good thing. It helps build their confidence and makes them feel valued. So, it doesn't seem like there's any moral issue here. I also think about the broader implications. If parents always told their children the truth, no matter how harsh, it could discourage them or make them feel bad about their efforts. By being supportive, parents are teaching their children the importance of kindness and encouragement, which are valuable life skills. In conclusion, telling a child you love their drawing, even if it's not your favorite, is a positive and morally acceptable action because it supports the child's emotional well-being and encourages creativity.
